questions.q: What does the COPY command's IAM_ROLE clause do?
options: Specifies the role Redshift assumes to read the source data from S3
Is optional and can always be omitted
Grants users permission to run the COPY command itself
Encrypts the data in transit only, with no bearing on access
questions.explain: COPY needs to read objects from S3, so it assumes an IAM role with s3:GetObject and s3:ListBucket permissions on the source location.

questions.q: Why does COPY dramatically outperform row-by-row INSERT for bulk loads?
options: COPY loads data in parallel across every compute node's slices; INSERT runs sequentially through the leader node
COPY skips data validation entirely, while INSERT validates every row
There is no real performance difference between them
COPY only works with CSV files, which are faster to parse than other formats
questions.explain: COPY's parallel load across all compute node slices is the core reason it scales for bulk loads in a way sequential INSERT statements never do.

questions.q: What problem does a manifest file solve that pointing COPY's FROM directly at an S3 prefix does not?
options: It lets you load an exact, explicit set of files, even if other objects land in the same prefix mid-load
It removes the need for an IAM role
It automatically converts CSV files to Parquet
It makes COPY run using row-by-row INSERT semantics
questions.explain: A manifest lists explicit S3 object URLs, so the load is precise and consistent even if the source prefix keeps changing.

questions.q: In a manifest file entry, what does setting "mandatory": true do?
options: Marks the file as optional and skippable
Fails the entire COPY load if that specific file is missing, instead of loading a partial dataset silently
Forces the file to load first, before any others
Has no effect on load behavior
questions.explain: Mandatory entries guarantee COPY either loads the complete expected batch or fails loudly, rather than silently loading a partial batch.

questions.q: Which clause tells COPY how to parse the structure of the source files (e.g. Parquet vs. CSV)?
options: MANIFEST
IAM_ROLE
FORMAT AS
DISTKEY
questions.explain: FORMAT AS specifies the source file format — PARQUET, CSV, JSON, AVRO, and others are supported.
